questions.stem: Why might a calorimetry experiment give a lower energy value than the true value for a food sample?

options.text: The food may not have been weighed correctly
Heat is lost to the surroundings instead of all going into the water
The water was too cold to absorb energy

questions.explanation: In a simple calorimetry experiment, a significant amount of heat escapes to the surroundings rather than being transferred to the water, resulting in a lower calculated energy value.
